- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.30 or higher) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially -0.30 or lower) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, then fails to revert to historical mean in later periods.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) and underestimate later (last 5–7 days), especially when sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is >0.20, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day; if sentiment < -0.20, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to counteract bias.
